Florida Gators cancel future football series with Notre Dame
stories.summary: Florida has canceled its 2031-32 football series against Notre Dame as the Gators adjust to the SEC's nine-game conference schedule. The two teams have only met once, with the Fighting Irish winning the 1992 Sugar Bowl, 39-28. The Gators will no longer visit the Irish on Nov. 15, 2031, nor will they host the Irish on Sept. 11, 2032. There will be no financial penalty for the update, as Florida negotiated a provision in its 2021 contract that allows the program to cancel in the event a nine-game SEC schedule was adopted. Florida previously eliminated future home-and-home agreements with Arizona State, California and North Carolina State.

stories.title: How will Tony Rojas' legacy be remembered?
stories.summary: Tony Rojas stands out at Penn State for his loyalty and defensive dominance in an era of NIL and transfers. It's fun discussing all of the accolades that Tony Rojas has compiled throughout his career, but it's the fact that they've all come with one program is much more laudatory. While Penn State has been up and down many peaks and valleys throughout his time with them, he never lost sight of what the program provided for him. In fact, the key reason he decided to stay with the team was not for money, but because he believed in the direction they were taking each and every year. It is that kind of leadership and legacy the Nittany Lions will miss.
